subject: DPA Annex: LLM telemetry minimization, retention tiers, and subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@healtech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@healtech.com, security@healtech.com
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: DPA annex clarifications: telemetry + retention

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Before we route to our legal team, our security/privacy team needs a short Q&A and a couple of artifacts to approve the annex for LLM telemetry. Can you confirm / provide the following: 

1) Telemetry minimization: which runtime telemetry fields are considered PII vs non-PII? We need an explicit list (examples: full prompt text, prompt metadata, user_id, session_id, anonymized hashes).
2) Retention tiers: proposed retention windows by data type (raw requests, KV cache snapshots, logs, metrics). We prefer explicit tier durations (e.g., 30d/90d/365d) and justification for LLM cache snapshots.
3) Subprocessor gating: what subprocessors may see request payloads or logs and under what conditions (support, debugging, training/analytics). Is there a process to request subprocessor exceptions?
4) Dataflow diagram: a visual that shows where request data is stored, cached, and egressed (including VPC/dedicated options).

If you can provide a short artifact pack (diagram + retention matrix + a short redaction playbook) that would help accelerate signoff. We are targeting a decision by EOD Wed (9 Jun).

Best,
Marta
Marta Delgado
Head of Security, HealTech

(Attachment: healtech-dpa-asks.pdf)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@healtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex clarifications: telemetry + retention

Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa and Grace from privacy/security to provide the artifacts and the technical rationale. Quick answers to set expectations: 

- Telemetry: by default, Redwood's hosted API does capture full request text and model output in logs for debugging and quality monitoring, but we have configurable minimization: prompt redaction hooks (PII scrubbing), user_id hashing, and optional request-only ephemeral mode (no persistent logs) for sensitive customers. We will provide a field-by-field map.
- Retention: we propose 30d for request logs by default, 90d for aggregated metrics, and optional 0d (ephemeral) for customers on Dedicated/Private or via a retention override. KV cache snapshots are retained only for the duration of an active session and purged after 24h by default unless the customer enables persistent session caching for performance.
- Subprocessors: typical subprocessors that may touch logs under support/debugging are our logging vendor (managed-hosted) and a telemetry analytics vendor — both under SOC 2 and covered in our subprocessors list. We have a gating process for exceptions that requires a security review + customer approval.

Marissa — can you prepare the artifacts Marta requested and include the proposed retention tiers and a short redaction playbook? Grace — can you add a dataflow diagram showing hosted vs dedicated/private paths and annotate who can access logs?

Rafael
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Direct: +1 415 555 0199)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex clarifications: telemetry + retention -- artifacts attached

Rafael / Grace — attaching the artifact pack per Marta's ask. Notes below: 

Attachments included: dpa_annex_proposal.pdf, dataflow_v2.drawio.png, retention_matrix.xlsx, redaction_playbook.md

Summary (field-level decisions):
- Field classification (PII vs non-PII): 
  * prompt_text: PII (may contain user identifiers/free text) — recommend mandatory redaction unless customer opts in.
  * model_response: PII (depends on content) — treated same as prompt_text for retention; can be excluded from logs in ephemeral mode.
  * user_id: treated as identifier — hashed with customer salt by default; can be pseudonymized.
  * session_id: non-identifying session token by default but included in logs for routing; rotate every 24h.
  * diagnostic_trace_id: non-PII.

- Retention tiers (defaults / options):
  * Request logs (full): 30 days default; option: 0 days (ephemeral) for Dedicated/Private or per-contract override.
  * Aggregated telemetry & metrics: 90 days default.
  * Audit logs (security events): 365 days (required for investigations).
  * KV cache snapshots: session-only (purge at session end) default; persistent cache only with explicit customer opt-in and retention policy (30 days max) documented in the annex.

- Subprocessor gating/process:
  * Subprocessors that may access logs: logging.storage@vendor (support only), telemetry-analytics@vendor (aggregated metrics). Both vendor contracts include SOC2 and restricted access.
  * Exception process: customer requests exception via contract amendment or security exception form -> security review -> documented mitigation -> customer approval. We propose adding a DPA clause referencing this gating flow.

- Redaction playbook (high level): 
  * Pre-ingest hooks: configure client-side scrubbing (recommended).
  * Server-side scrubbing: configurable regex/PII detectors + manual review beacon.
  * Post-collection hashing: user identifiers salted per-customer.

Grace — dataflow_v2.drawio.png shows two paths: Hosted (Redwood control plane + shared logging bucket with retention policies) and Dedicated/Private (customer-managed VPC, optional KMS for key custody). I annotated subprocessors and where data egress may occur.

I included short justification paragraphs in the PDF so legal has something to cite. Happy to iterate after you get feedback from HealTech.

Marissa Cole
Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference

(Attachment stubs: dpa_annex_proposal.pdf, dataflow_v2.drawio.png, retention_matrix.xlsx, redaction_playbook.md)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@healtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, contracts@healtech.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex clarifications: telemetry + retention

Marta — attaching the artifact pack Marissa prepared and Grace's annotated dataflow. Key callouts up front:

- We mark prompt_text and model_response as potentially PII by default and recommend customers enable redaction hooks unless they explicitly allow retention.
- Default retention windows: request logs 30d, metrics 90d, audit logs 365d, KV cache session-only. We can contractually reduce request log retention to 0 days (ephemeral) for customers on Dedicated/Private or with an annex.
- Subprocessor gating: any subprocessor access to request payloads requires a documented request + security review + customer OK. We will add a short clause to the DPA annex describing the gating flow and list the named subprocessors.

Artifacts (linked/included): dpa_annex_proposal.pdf, dataflow_v2.drawio.png, retention_matrix.xlsx, redaction_playbook.md
Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-raf-healtech-dpa
DocuSign (proposed annex envelope): DocuSign://envelope/0a1b2c3d

Next steps: if this aligns with HealTech's expectations, can we get a quick legal review and confirm whether you want the 0d ephemeral retention option for production? If yes, we'll prepare an annex redline for signature.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
